author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the secret to attracting and retaining great people has less to do with perks and policies, and more to do with how a company tells its story, builds its culture, and makes people feel they belong? Many organizations treat hiring and retention as separate challenges, when in reality they are deeply connected.

In this talk, Shanda Lee shares why the same principles used to win customers can also win talent. Drawing from more than 25 years of executive leadership in marketing and culture, she reveals how companies can create stronger brands internally and externally to attract the right people, keep top performers engaged, and build cultures where employees thrive.

Through real-world insight and practical strategies, Shanda challenges leaders to rethink outdated silos and see people strategy as a growth strategy. Because the companies that win tomorrow will be the ones that learn how to market opportunity, lead with purpose, and create workplaces worth staying for. Shanda Lee
title: The cheat code to hiring (and keeping) great people | Shanda Lee | TEDxEustis

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if technology could give humans new senses—detecting disease before we feel sick or revealing signals we were never evolved to perceive? This talk explores how nature’s extraordinary sensing abilities can be connected to chips, opening a future in which we can sense the invisible. https://sites.ucsd.edu/aran-lab/ #TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #TEDtalks #FutureTechnology #Biotechnology #HumanSenses Dr. Kiana Aran is a Professor of Bioengineering and Medicine at the University of California San Diego whose work bridges biology and modern electronic systems. Born and raised in Iran and trained in electrical and biomedical engineering in United States, she pioneers bioelectronic sensing platforms that directly interface with living systems. She is best known for inventing CRISPR-Chip, a technology enabling real-time, amplification-free genetic detection and precision gene-editing analysis. Her research focuses on multiomics sensing and technologies for precision biology and medicine. Dr. Aran
title: Giving Humans New Senses Through Technology | Kiana Aran | TEDxSanDiego

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this talk, Prabha Ramaswamy reflects on the uniqueness of the Province of Saskatchewan in Canada and the stories that shape our sense of place. She invites us to see the province with fresh eyes, not only for what it is, but for what it can become. Prabha Ramaswamy is a champion of Saskatchewan business, a visionary leader, and a passionate community builder. With a Master’s in Social Work and over 30 years of experience, she has guided organizations through change to achieve strategic growth and impact. Before joining the Saskatchewan Chamber of Commerce, she served as CEO of WESK, launching initiatives to support entrepreneurs and close the gender gap.

Prior to WESK, Prabha served as CEO of the Accounting Designation, Certified General Accountants of Saskatchewan. She was part of the provincial merger committee responsible for unifying the profession to create Certified Professional Accountants of Saskatchewan. She was conferred an honorary CPA for her work on unifying the accou
title: Why the World Needs Saskatchewan | Prabha Ramaswamy | TEDxRegina

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Artificial intelligence can now create paintings, films, stories, and other works that are often difficult to distinguish from those created by humans. As these technologies become more common, they are forcing us to rethink some of our assumptions about creativity and artistic expression.

Drawing on his background in artificial intelligence and digital media, Damian Schofield explores how we judge art and why we connect with certain works. He invites us to consider a question that is becoming increasingly relevant: when a piece of art moves us, does it matter who or what created it? Dr. Schofield is Director of Human Computer Interaction (Full Professor) at SUNY Oswego, a role he has held since 2009, and Adjunct Associate Professor of Forensic Computing at Edith Cowan University in Perth, Australia. Previously, he was Associate Professor of Computer Games and Digital Media at RMIT University in Melbourne and Lecturer in Computer Science at the University of Nottingham, UK. He is als
title: Finding inspiration in art among all the digital noise | Damian Schofield | TEDxSUNY Oswego

author: TEDx Talks
description: The Appeal of the Ordinary questions our obsession with the extraordinary. In a world where success is increasingly measured by visibility, achievement, and being noticed, what happens when a student chooses the ordinary instead? Perhaps our expectations for our children’s lives are shaped less by what makes them happy and more by what makes them visible. Maybe there is value, freedom, and even courage I'm a 10th grader, forever curious, always asking why, and finding fun in the wonderfully weird. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Appeal of the Ordinary | Aira Nigam | TEDxThe Ardee School NFC

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if you don’t have to be “naturally gifted” to belong in STEM? Data scientist Chen Siwen shares her journey of confronting gender stereotypes, self-doubt, and the pressure to be perfect. From struggling with computer science to pursuing advanced training and building a career in data science, she learned that talent is not simply something we are born with—it can grow through curiosity, persistence, and the courage to keep exploring. She introduces her personal TIE framework: Talent, Integrity, and Empowerment, and argues that our potential becomes even more powerful when we use it to empower others. Her message is simple: you do not need to be perfect, extraordinary, or fearless to begin. You only need to be willing to try, fail, learn, and start again. Chen Siwen is a data scientist passionate about the intersection of data, technology, and business. Her academic and professional journey has taken her across multiple fields, including computer science, while challenging her own
title: Talent × Integrity × Empowerment: Becoming the Light You Need | Siwen Chen | TEDxSWFLA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if we stopped letting society write our roles for us?

In this talk, Jinhan He explores how theater can become a tool for understanding ourselves, challenging expectations, and creating new possibilities in life. Drawing from her own journey in theater education and her experiences working with young people, she reflects on self-awareness, personal agency, and the courage to take action when the path ahead is uncertain.

Through stories from her work, Jinhan shows how theater can help people break free from fixed labels, express emotions, challenge gender expectations, and discover different dimensions of themselves. Ultimately, she invites us to see life as a stage—not one with a predetermined script, but one where we can choose our roles, create new possibilities, and write our own stories. Jinhan He is the Founder of Uni and Shanghai Uni You Ni You Qi Culture Media, the East China Regional Director of Beijing Guanglu Culture Communication, and Co-Founder of Shenghuo Shiguang.
title: Life as a Stage: Rewrite Your Own Script | Jinhan He | TEDxSWFLA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: For more than two decades, lawyer and anti-domestic-violence advocate Li Ying has stood alongside survivors of domestic violence. Through stories drawn from hundreds of cases, she reveals why leaving an abusive relationship is rarely as simple as “just walking away”—and how economic dependence, social stigma, psychological trauma, and gaps in support systems can trap survivors in cycles of violence. From individual cases to the development of China’s Anti-Domestic Violence Law, Li Ying reflects on the progress that has been made and the work that remains. Ultimately, she invites each of us to become a small light in the darkness: to speak up, offer support, and help create a future where every life can breathe freely. Li Ying is a lawyer, advocate, and longtime leader in the fight against domestic violence in China. With more than 23 years of experience, she has provided legal support to hundreds of survivors and conducted nearly 10,000 legal consultations. Through her legal practice
title: Walking Toward Spring: Breaking the Silence Around Domestic Violence | Ying Li | TEDxSWFLA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens when a life that looks successful from the outside no longer feels meaningful from within? Diana Guo shares her journey from a high-pressure career in finance to a life shaped by self-discovery, photography, travel, and deeper connection with the world. Beginning with a simple conversation with her therapist, she gradually learned to reconnect with her emotions, challenge society’s definition of success, and find meaning beyond achievement. Through her idea of the “Hero’s Journey,” Diana invites us to see transformation not as a single turning point, but as a continuous process of questioning, exploring, and becoming. Because the most important journey may not be toward becoming someone else—but toward becoming yourself. DIANA GUO is a private banker, photographer, and lifelong explorer of the human experience.
With more than 15 years of experience in private banking, she has worked closely with renowned entrepreneurs and high-net-worth individuals around the world, gaini
title: Hey! Are You Ready to Embark on Your Own Hero's Journey? | Diana Guo | TEDxSWFLA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Edge of the Ordinary explores how every generation has its own idea of what “ordinary” means. What seems normal to one generation can feel completely different to the next. For today’s young people, the gap is wider than ever, shaped by technology, changing expectations, and a world that constantly tells them to be more, do more, and stand out. Hi! My name is Niyaati and I am in Year 5. I am curious, creative, and always eager to learn, with a love for chess, music, basketball, and exploring new ideas. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Edge of the Ordinary | Niyaati Fernandes | TEDxThe Ardee School NFC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We turn on a tap and water appears. But behind that simple act lies a river, land, labour, communities, and consequences we rarely see.

Drawing from his life along the Cauvery and his experience working with communities to restore water bodies, Ashok Raja asks us to look at progress through four simple questions:

What does it give us?
What does it hide from us?
Who pays the cost?
What choices does it leave for the next generation?

Through water, the talk explores a larger conversation about social justice, climate justice, and intergenerational justice — and asks how we can build progress without taking away the choices of those who come after us.
 Ashok Raja is a Climate Activist and Community Mobilizer from Tamil Nadu, India.He has led the community-driven restoration of 15 water bodies that had remained dry or severely neglected for over a decade by bringing together local residents, volunteers, institutions, and organizations through citizen-led action. He founded the Stop Scre
title: The River Behind the Tap | Ashok Raja | TEDxWestberry School Tenali Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Every big achievement begins as an idea that may look like delusion to others. Through my entrepreneurial journey, I share why going from 0 to 1 is the hardest stage, how moving from 1 to 10 becomes easier, and why growing beyond that is possible only through a strong team, shared belief, and collective effort. Parveen Padalkar is an ET 40 Under 40 – South awardee and recipient of the Digital Women Awards by SheThePeople. She is the Founder of Ekori, a handloom fashion enterprise that brings together traditional Indian weaves and modern fabrics, while working closely with weavers and artisans.

An entrepreneur passionate about preserving India’s textile heritage, Parveen is building a modern business around sustainable slow fashion, making traditional craftsmanship relevant to today’s consumer. She has also been a speaker at multiple industry and entrepreneurship events. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local communit
title: The World behind words - Misconception | Parveen: Padalkar | TEDxWestberry School Tenali Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The Unscripted Future explores how leaders can navigate organisational change when the future cannot be predicted. Through the 4Ps of change—Purpose, People, Process and Performance—and the River Leadership Model—Anchor, Read, Respond, Reinvent—the talk shows how leaders can stay grounded in purpose while adapting to uncertainty.

The Tedx talk also explains how you cannot script the future. But you can build the mindset, people and organisation that are ready to navigate it.
 Sivamalani Sivaraj is a strategic technology and transformation leader with over two decades of experience driving business transformation, delivery excellence, and high-performing teams across BFSI and retail. As a Vice President at Commonwealth Bank, she brings together people, processes, technology, and innovation to turn complex challenges into meaningful outcomes. Known for her ability to make the impossible possible, she is an expert in building empowered, high-performing teams and transforming challenges
title: The World behind words - Misconception | Sivamalani Sivaraj | TEDxWestberry School Tenali Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if ownership is not something we inherit, but something we learn by experiencing it?
In this talk, Ankush Mehrotra traces a deeply personal journey from childhood lessons and his father's quiet acts of trust, to entrepreneurship, failure, leadership, relationships, mentoring, and the responsibility of caring for others.
From paying a family dinner bill with money secretly handed to him by his father, to building businesses, surviving the uncertainty of the 2020 lockdown, learning leadership through a dream of joining the Air Force, recognising ownership in a student, and eventually passing that same lesson on to his cousin, Ankush explores one simple idea:
Give people something meaningful to own, and they discover what they are capable of.
This is a talk about growing up, taking responsibility, beginning again, and eventually passing that sense of ownership on to someone else.
What will you own?

What will you build?

And when you're strong enough, what will you pass on?
Think it
title: Ownership- The skill we forgot to teach | Ankush Mehrotra | TEDxWestberry School Tenali Youth

description:
Talk Description:
A raw, personal account of turning repeated setbacks, loss, financial hardship, and failed ventures into the foundation for building Social Sculpt and Nebula Startup School. Arun traces his journey from being an 18-year-old with nothing to becoming a founder and TEDx speaker, showing how resilience and consistent action (not luck) turn life's hardest moments into growth. The talk closes with his signature line: "If I can sculpt it, you can too."
 Arunachalam S is a Chennai-based serial entrepreneur and personal branding strategist helping founders, doctors, and executives build authority on LinkedIn. He leads Social Sculpt, an agency working with hospitals, startups, and personal brands, and co-founded Nebula Startup School, a founder education platform. He also built PostAutopsy, a LinkedIn content intelligence tool used by creators worldwide, and runs Social Sculpt Academy, training the next generation of marketers. Also hosts the Sculptors Podcast, built on the be
title: Juggling Lemons: Go Against the Flow | Arunachalam S | TEDxWestberry School Tenali Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens when the success you have worked towards no longer feels like enough? In this talk, the speaker explores how our definition of winning can change. Medals, gold and public applause offer visible recognition, yet reaching those milestones may not bring the fulfilment we imagined. She reflects on the courage it takes to reconsider what matters and choose a different direction, even when others still celebrate the path we are on. Her message invites us to make room for quieter, more personal victories: a life shaped by purpose, choices that reflect who we are, and fulfilment that does not depend on an audience. Dr Phathokuhle Zondi is a Sport and Exercise Medicine specialist with over a decade of experience working in elite sport. She has cared for athletes at Olympic, Paralympic and Commonwealth Games, and currently advises the International Olympic Committee on athlete health.

She is Chief Specialist for Sports Medicine at UKZN and chairs Rugby Africa's Women's Health Subc
title: When winning changes meaning | Dr Phathokuhle Zondi | TEDxDurban

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Markel explora la perseverancia como una disciplina que se construye mediante el esfuerzo diario, la práctica y el aprendizaje de los errores. A partir de su experiencia con el ajedrez, relata cómo las repetidas derrotas frente a su padre lo impulsaron a tomar clases y mejorar hasta conseguir ganarle por primera vez.

También utiliza el proceso de desarrollo de James Dyson para ilustrar la importancia de seguir perfeccionando una idea después de intentos fallidos. Su mensaje central es que perseguir un objetivo exige actuar con constancia y estar dispuesto a aprender durante el camino. Esta idea anima a la audiencia a entender los reveses como parte del aprendizaje y a reconocer el crecimiento personal que surge del esfuerzo sostenido. Soy un estudiante de secundaria que actualmente está en 2º de la ESO y tiene 13 años. title: No te rindas | Markel Zabala | TEDxYouth@CRC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The landscape of modern medicine has undergone a profound transformation, shifting its focus from merely extending life to actively preserving its quality. Nowhere is this revolution more evident than in rheumatology. Historically, diagnoses like rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or ankylosing spondylitis carried a grim prognosis of relentless pain, joint destruction, and ultimate disability. Early treatments relied heavily on high-dose steroids, which often caused side effects as devastating as the diseases themselves. Today, however, biotechnology has rewritten this narrative, transforming once-debilitating conditions into highly manageable illnesses.
The cornerstone of this triumph is the shift from broad immunosuppression to precision medicine. Traditional therapies acted like a sledgehammer, weakening the entire immune system. In contrast, modern Biologic Disease-Modifying Anti-Rheumatic Drugs (bDMARDs) and JAK inhibitors function as guided missiles. They precisely target and block th
title: The changing landscape of rheumatology | Dr. Gaurav Jain | TEDxHauz Khas

author: TEDx Talks
description: In her talk, Maithili examines why the speed at which we build has come to matter more than what we actually build. Drawing on her experience as an architect, she contrasts a digital "Tron world," where structures appear and vanish at the click of a button, with Rani Ki Vav, an eleventh-century stepwell in Gujarat that still cools the skin and holds the marks of centuries of hands. She makes the case that architecture only matters when it builds real human connection rather than solving a function fast, challenging her audience to build things that can't be undone. Maithili Raut is a co-founder and partner at reD Architects, a Mumbai-based design studio that prioritizes research while creating buildings and environments.  Holding a Master’s degree in Architecture and Urban Design from Columbia University, she has worked in New York, Paris and Mumbai. Maithili Raut applies multidisciplinary methodologies to her work. Maithili Raut’s work spans from restoration projects, master planning
title: The Spirit of a Place | Maithili Raut | TEDxDAIS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: The speech by Sukriti is about rediscovering India through stories that are often overlooked or forgotten. She talks about India’s rich history in fashion, the story of Maratha admiral Kanhoji Angre, ancient ideas of technology and India’s connection to dinosaurs. These stories changed the way she saw India and made her realise that there is much more to the country than the negative stories we usually hear. The speech is really about how the things we don’t see or know about can completely change the way we understand a place and connect with it. It ends with the idea that the stories we tell about India shape the way we imagine and build its future. Sukriti, a DAIS alumna, is an author, screenwriter, entrepreneur, and founder of Unibrow Stories. A graduate of the London School of Economics and Political Science and a Master of Fine Arts in Creative Nonfiction from Columbia University, her work has been published in leading international publications including Vox, Quartz, The Hindu,
title: From Shame to Joy | Sukriti YJ | TEDxDAIS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Empathy quietly holds families, classrooms, and communities together, yet modern pressures are steadily eroding it. What happens when we stop reading each other's faces? Can a chatbot's comfort replace a human's presence? Drawing from her experience as a DAIS psychology teacher, Ms Richa Chauhan traces empathy's evolutionary roots in mirror neurones through its measurable decline in the social-media era, and makes the case for why real human empathy remains essential to how families, schools, and societies function. For over 15 years, Ms. Richa Chauhan has devoted herself to helping young people understand not just psychology, but themselves. Her journey through leading international schools — including Singapore International School, Mumbai, and École Mondiale World School — has shaped her into an educator who sees teaching as an act of care as much as instruction. Today, at Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Mumbai, she serves as Psychology and TOK Educator, Psychology Subject L
title: The Invisible Bridge | Richa Chauhan | TEDxDAIS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In his talk, Rajvir challenges the widely held belief that confidence is something visible, worn on the outside as steady hands or fearless body language. Drawing on his experience cycling sixteen hundred kilometres into the Himalayas and addressing fifteen hundred students as a Head Boy candidate, both moments where his hands shook uncontrollably despite being seen as one of the most confident people in the room. He discusses that confidence was never meant to guarantee an outcome, only to get someone to the starting line, and argues that we’ve been mistaking the visible signs of composure for something that was always meant to be felt, not seen. Rajvir Jagwani is a 17-year-old Grade 12 student at DAIS who is passionate about public speaking, debate, and making life a little easier for himself and those around him. An accomplished public speaker and debater, he has chaired over ten Model UN conferences and competed in more than twenty others, and served as Head Boy of JNS. When he’s
title: Two Lies, One Truth About Confidence | Rajvir Jagwani | TEDxDAIS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: A founder puts an impossible number on the table in a room that wanted a safe one. Three months later she is probably going to miss it, and she would say it again. This talk is about what happens in the long silent stretch after you go against the room: why the right hard decisions feel like peace rather than adrenaline, why panic is the more expensive risk, and why going against the flow turns out to have less to do with courage than with finding the few people you never have to perform for. Disha Bhatnagar is the Co-Founder of Growify Digital LLP and Founder of Lookify, an AI-powered virtual try-on platform. Starting her entrepreneurial journey at 17, she has built Growify into a leading digital growth partner for 120+ luxury and fashion brands, including Rohit Bal, Rahul Mishra, House of Masaba and Tarun Tahiliani. She has led a 100+ member team and driven AI-powered solutions across e-commerce, customer experience and digital operations. Her work sits at the intersection of AI, fa
title: You Will Not Have It All. You Will Have Enough | Disha Bhatnagar | TEDxWestberry School Tenali Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this TEDx talk, Matisa Mallbris explores the powerful connection between language and
identity, and addresses how something as ordinary as the words we use can shape our sense of
belonging, culture, personality, and self-image. From the languages we inherit to the words we
choose for ourselves, language doesn't simply express who we are; it can help shape who we
believe ourselves to be. Growing up in international environments, Matisa believes that language is more than a tool we use to communicate, it is one of the ways we understand ourselves and the people around us. The words we speak, the languages we grow up with, and even the labels others give us can influence how we see our identity and how we believe others see us. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Beyond Communication: How Language Shapes Identity | Matisa Mallbris | TEDxCanadian Academy Youth

description:
Meet Sayuri Tsuchitani, Founder of Sumo Yoga, and speaker of “The Art of Monozukuri: A Japanese Philosophy for Meaningful Life.”

What if the true measure of life is not what we own, but the value we create?

Through these experiences, she reveals how purpose, care, and meaningful creation can transform not only our work, but also the way we live and connect with others. As a message to students, Sayuri reminds us: “Your future is not something you find—it is something you create.”

With a whimsical outlook on life and a passion for personal growth, Pamela invites us to explore authenticity, self-awareness, and the journey of becoming our truest selves. What if the lies we tell aren’t just acts of deception, but invitations to grow?

description: What if the strongest foundations are the ones people rarely notice? In this powerful TEDx talk, Rahul Koti explores the often-overlooked role of branding in India’s steel and construction industry, sharing how business can move beyond selling a product to building trust, creating value, and earning a place in people’s minds. Through Ctrl + Alt + Create, he shows how controlling the story, altering perceptions, and creating lasting trust can transform a product into a brand and a business into a legacy Rahul Ashok Koti is an Indian entrepreneur and business leader, serving as the Director of KOTI STEEL, a leading TMT steel manufacturer based in Hubballi, Karnataka. With a BBA from India and a Master's in International Business Management from the United Kingdom, he brings a global perspective to business growth and brand building. title: Branding the Backbone of India | Mr. Rahul Ashok Koti | TEDxBirla Intl School Youth

description:
Vaneeza Ahmed opens with the questions she is repeatedly asked about her appearance, then turns to a deeper question: how do beliefs shape the way we live? She recounts her father’s death, the unexpected route that led her into modelling and acting, periods of serious illness, motherhood, and the grief that followed her sister’s death. She describes how loss and fear narrowed her life, and how therapy, reflection and a fresh start helped her look inward again. Ahmed speaks from personal experience about faith, gratitude, self-talk and the pressure to meet other people’s expectations. Her closing appeal is to live more deliberately in the present, care for oneself and seek an authentic life. She asks listeners to question beliefs learned in childhood and the stories they tell themselves

author: TEDx Talks
description: Sabeen Hamood was told she could be a good person or a champion, but not both. After winning Best Delegate at Harvard National Model United Nations, she found that praise carried another burden: other people’s ideas about who she should be. As a student, eldest daughter and Pakistani woman, she faced expectations that often contradicted one another. In this interactive talk, she asks the audience to name the labels others give them, imagine the “ideal” woman, and then describe themselves without those outside voices. The last question proves hardest. Hamood examines why identity can become a response to achievement, family roles and judgment, and offers a different question to guide personal growth: who am I becoming? Her message is an invitation to reclaim the language used to define us and make present choices in line with the person we want to become.  Sabeen Hamood is a public speaking coach and a member of the LUMS Model United Nations delegation. LUMS reports that she won Best D
title: Between Who I Am and Who I’m Becoming | Sabeen Hamood | TEDxFCCU Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Bushra Ansari has lived through a remarkable shift in how people connect, from handwritten letters and the household telephone to social media and artificial intelligence. With humour and stories from her family and career, she describes the unease of learning new technologies while trying to keep pace with younger generations. She also speaks candidly about age, online criticism, her changing personal life, and the many creative paths she has followed as a singer, actor, comedian, writer and host. None of those turns, she suggests, had to be planned in advance. Her invitation to young people is to keep exploring their abilities, welcome change without hiding who they are, and protect their happiness as they build their lives. At 70, she still measures youth by curiosity and spirit.
 Actress, Comedian, Singer, Playwright This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Staying Young in Spirit | Bushra Ansari | TEDxFCCU Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Irtifa Nasir appears comfortable teaching and speaking to groups, yet she admits that fear of judgment and public speaking still follows her onto the TEDx stage. She explores how social expectations teach people, especially women, to avoid uncertainty, take up less space and silence parts of themselves. For Nasir, courage means acting while fear is present and letting care for others guide the decision. She traces that belief to the support she received from her family and to the pandemic isolation that led her to found The Tinkers’ Collective. Through art, play and shared experiences, the community offers people a place to connect and support one another. Nasir closes with a practical question for difficult moments: is this choice rooted in fear, or in love?
 Marketing Professional, Educator, Entrepreneur, Mentor This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Choose Love Over Fear | Irtifa Nasir | TEDxFCCU Women
